habitat: Firefish, also known as dartfish, inhabit coral reefs of the Indo-Pacific, from the Red Sea and East Africa to the Hawaiian Islands and the Great Barrier Reef. They are found at depths of 5-20 meters, living in burrows in sandy areas adjacent to reef structures. They prefer areas with moderate current and clear water. Firefish are planktivores, feeding on zooplankton drifting past their burrow entrances. They hover above their burrows facing into the current, darting back into their shelter at the slightest sign of danger.
diet: Firefish are planktivores, feeding primarily on zooplankton including copepods, amphipods, crustacean larvae, and fish eggs drifting in the water column. They feed by hovering a few centimeters above their burrow, facing into the current to intercept passing food particles. They are daytime feeders, retreating into burrows at night. In reef aquariums, they accept a variety of prepared foods including brine shrimp, mysis shrimp, and finely chopped seafood. Their feeding behavior is graceful and deliberate, making them a favorite among reefkeepers.
behavior: Firefish are peaceful, timid fish that live in monogamous pairs or small groups. They construct and maintain burrows in the sand that serve as both shelter and sleeping quarters. When threatened, they perform a characteristic 'dart' — a rapid, almost instantaneous retreat into their burrow, which gives them their alternate name 'dartfish.' They are territorial but rarely aggressive toward other species. Firefish communicate through body posture and fin displays. Their courtship involves elaborate fin-spreading and dancing displays by the male.
facts: The firefish gets its name from its spectacular coloration: a white anterior body that transitions to brilliant red, orange, and yellow toward the tail, with elongated dorsal fin rays that flicker like flames. These elongated dorsal fin rays can be raised and lowered to signal mood — fully erect when excited or displaying, flattened when resting. They grow to 7-9 centimeters in length. Firefish are among the most popular marine aquarium fish due to their beauty, small size, and peaceful nature. They can live 3-5 years in captivity with proper care.
naming: Firefish names might reflect their fiery coloration or darting behavior. Consider names like Ember, Flash, Torch, Spark, Blaze, Flame, Flicker, Dart, Comet, Phoenix, Coralie, Inferno, Scorch, Zippy, or Helios (sun god).
